cues.en: Okay, yeah, so my name is Greg.
cues.zh: 好的，大家好，我叫 Greg。

cues.en: I work for a company called Table XI in Chicago, where a 30-person rail shop.
cues.zh: 我在芝加哥一家叫 Table XI 的公司工作，我们是一家 30 人的 Rails 团队。

cues.en: I've been programming most of my life.
cues.zh: 我大半辈子都在写代码。

cues.zh: 我大概六七岁的时候，就开始在 TRS 80 上编程了。

cues.zh: 那时候我有磁带，上面装了 BASIC 语言。

cues.zh: 我记得有本叫《321 Contact》的杂志，每个月都会寄来，上面有 BASIC 程序，

cues.en: in the back page.
cues.zh: 就印在封底上。

cues.en: and sit there and wouldn't copy and paste or literally copy the program into the thing
cues.zh: 我就坐在那儿，没法复制粘贴，只能老老实实把程序一行行敲进去，

cues.en: and run it and just make the screen change colors and whatnot.
cues.zh: 运行起来，让屏幕变个颜色什么的。

cues.en: I spent most of my professional career kind of straddling development and client-facing
cues.zh: 我的大部分职业生涯，都在兼顾技术开发和面向客户的

cues.en: work.
cues.zh: 业务工作。

cues.zh: 同时，我还患有双相情感障碍 II 型和 ADD（注意力缺陷障碍）。

cues.zh: 别跟昨天 Matt 说的“纪念日驱动开发”搞混了，我指的是注意力

cues.en: deficit disorder.
cues.zh: 缺陷障碍。

cues.en: Today I want to tell you guys my story.
cues.zh: 今天我想给大家讲讲我的故事。

cues.zh: 我想告诉大家，为什么我们需要在办公室里、

cues.zh: 在同行之间、在技术聚会上，以及像这样的会议中，更多地探讨抑郁症和心理健康问题。

cues.en: You might be familiar with type 1 bipolar.
cues.zh: 大家可能对 I 型双相情感障碍比较熟悉。

cues.en: It's also called manic depression.
cues.zh: 它也被称为躁郁症。

cues.en: It means that you cycle between periods of mania, the good parts, and depression at
cues.zh: 这意味着你会在躁狂期（亢奋状态）和处于低谷的

cues.en: the bottom.
cues.zh: 抑郁期之间循环交替。

cues.en: The mania can feel kind of euphoric, and it can also be incredibly destructive because
cues.zh: 躁狂期可能会让人感觉非常亢奋，但它同时也极具破坏性，因为

cues.en: it leads to great impulsiveness, people make a lot of bad decisions at that time.
cues.zh: 它会导致极度的冲动，让人在那个时候做出许多糟糕的决定。

cues.en: For type 1 bipolar, this can also be rapid cycling, so you can go quickly from top to
cues.zh: 对于 I 型双相情感障碍，这还可能是快速循环的，也就是说，你会非常迅速地从峰顶跌落到

cues.en: bottom very fast.
cues.zh: 谷底。

cues.en: My bipolar, type 2 bipolar, is much milder, and the cycles tend to be much more elongated.
cues.zh: 而我的双相障碍，也就是 II 型双相，症状要温和得多，并且循环周期往往也拉得更长。

cues.en: So what it would look like for me is typically anywhere from 4 to 12 weeks or so of just this long, slow, gradual slide down.
cues.zh: 对我来说，这通常表现为持续4到12周左右漫长、缓慢且逐渐下滑的过程。

cues.en: It felt for me like I was always trying to crawl up a gravel incline that was really steep,
cues.zh: 我感觉自己就像一直在攀爬一段非常陡峭的碎石坡，

cues.en: and no matter how hard I spun my wheels, I just kept sliding back down further and further.
cues.zh: 无论车轮怎么拼命打转，我都只是不断往后滑，越滑越深。

cues.en: And this was quite frustrating for me.
cues.zh: 这让我感到非常沮丧。

cues.en: I first noticed this during my last year,
cues.zh: 我第一次注意到这种情况是在我读大学的最后一年，

cues.en: my fifth year, my victory lap,
cues.zh: 也就是第五年，我延毕的那一年，

cues.en: though it wasn't particularly victorious for me,
cues.zh: 虽然对我来说并不怎么光彩，

cues.en: at the University of Illinois.
cues.zh: 那是在伊利诺伊大学。

cues.en: And I had just broken up with a girlfriend,
cues.zh: 当时我刚和女友分手，

cues.en: I had just moved into a place by my own,
cues.zh: 刚搬进一个人的住处，

cues.en: my first time living without any roommates.
cues.zh: 第一次没有室友一起住。

cues.en: I was on my way to failing out of school.
cues.zh: 我当时快要被学校退学了。

cues.en: And things were just getting really rough for me.
cues.zh: 日子对我来说变得特别艰难。

cues.en: I was never a particularly good student,
cues.zh: 我从来都不是个特别优秀的学生，

cues.en: but I was always kind of smart enough
cues.zh: 但我总还算挺聪明的，

cues.en: that I could kind of fake my way through it.
cues.zh: 总能一路糊弄过去。

cues.en: But that started catching up to me my junior-senior year.
cues.zh: 但到了大三、大四，这套就行不通了。

cues.en: It turns out that if you're going to go in and take a linear algebra final, it helps
cues.zh: 事实证明，如果你要去参加线性代数期末考试，

cues.en: if you actually know what linear algebra means.
cues.zh: 你最好真懂线性代数是什么意思。

cues.en: I've taken that class twice now, I still couldn't tell you.
cues.zh: 那门课我都修了两次，现在依然说不上来。

cues.en: And it became pretty obvious that I wasn't going to make it, that I wasn't going to
cues.zh: 显然我撑不下去了，我没法

cues.en: graduate, and I didn't know how to tell my parents about that.
cues.zh: 顺利毕业，而我不知道该怎么跟父母开口。

cues.en: And I didn't know how to deal with the fact that everybody else around me seemed to be
cues.zh: 身边其他人似乎都能顺顺利利毕业，

cues.en: graduating just fine, but I wasn't.
cues.zh: 就我做不到，我不知道该怎么面对这件事。

cues.en: I had a friend who said, Greg is one of the smartest guys
cues.zh: 我有个朋友曾说：Greg 是我认识的人里最聪明的之一，

cues.en: I know, but he also just happens to be one of the
cues.zh: 但他碰巧也是我认识的人里

cues.en: laziest people I know, and I believed that shit.
cues.zh: 最懒的一个，而我当时居然信了这套鬼话。

cues.en: Because I didn't have any other excuse for it.
cues.zh: 因为我找不出任何其他借口。

cues.en: I slept all day.
cues.zh: 我整天都在睡觉。

cues.en: I didn't go to class.
cues.zh: 我翘课了。

cues.en: I knew that I was mentally capable, or at least smart
cues.zh: 我知道自己的脑子没问题，或者至少

cues.en: enough to go to class and do the homework.
cues.zh: 聪明到足够去上课和写作业。

cues.en: I just wasn't doing it, and that sounds
cues.zh: 可我就是不去做，而在我看来

cues.en: like laziness to me.
cues.zh: 这听起来就是懒惰。

cues.en: I pretty much, when I'm at the bottom of the depression,
cues.zh: 当我深陷抑郁低谷时，

cues.en: and I sleep a lot, I'd say it's the most obvious symptom.
cues.zh: 通常睡得特别多，我觉得这是最明显的症状。

cues.en: The best part of my day back then
cues.zh: 那时我一天中最美好的时光，

cues.en: was the time in which I was unconscious,
cues.zh: 就是失去意识睡着的时候，

cues.en: and the time I didn't have to deal with reality
cues.zh: 那段时间我不用去面对堆积如山的现实，

cues.en: that was piling up, and then just physically,
cues.zh: 而且在身体上，

cues.en: it just was so hard to get out of bed,
cues.zh: 下床实在太困难了，

cues.en: I'd oversleep my alarm.
cues.zh: 闹钟响了我也起不来。

cues.en: I'd stop going to class, I'd stop going to work.
cues.zh: 我不再去上课，也不去上班了。

cues.en: I had a part-time job with a very flexible schedule,
cues.zh: 我当时有一份时间很灵活的兼职，

cues.en: and it took them a while to realize
cues.zh: 他们过了好一阵子才察觉到

cues.en: that I had pretty much stopped coming in.
cues.zh: 我基本上已经不去上班了。

cues.en: And I had a friend, though, a co-worker who was just a great friend, and he really cared,
cues.zh: 但我有一个朋友，也是同事，他人特别好，而且真心关心我，

cues.en: who's concerned, and he had sent me a couple emails just saying, hey, Greg, what's going
cues.zh: 他很担心我，就给我发了几封邮件，问我：“嘿，Greg，发生什么

cues.en: on, you know?
cues.zh: 事了？”

cues.en: And I ignored them, because I didn't know how to talk to them about it.
cues.zh: 我没有理会，因为我不知道该怎么跟他说这事。

cues.en: And then one day, it was like 2 o'clock on like a Tuesday, I got a phone call from Bill,
cues.zh: 后来有一天，大概是周二下午两点左右，我接到了 Bill 的电话，

cues.en: and I was still in bed, and I ignored it.
cues.zh: 当时我还躺在床上，就没接。

cues.en: And then he called again, and I ignored it again.
cues.zh: 接着他又打来一次，我还是没接。

cues.en: And then I heard a knock at my door.
cues.zh: 然后我就听到了敲门声。

cues.en: I was like, hey, Greg, it's Bill.
cues.zh: 门外喊着：“嘿，Greg，我是 Bill。”

cues.en: I was like, shit, it's fine.
cues.zh: 我当时心想：靠，没事。

cues.en: Just be quiet.
cues.zh: 安静点就行。

cues.en: He doesn't need to know I'm here besides Tuesday at two.
cues.zh: 他又不知道我在这里，而且这可是周二下午两点。

cues.en: Why would he even think I'm here anyway?
cues.zh: 他怎么可能会觉得我在家呢？

cues.en: And then I heard the door knob start to turn.
cues.zh: 然后我听到门把手开始转动了。

cues.en: I wasn't very good at locking my doors back then.
cues.zh: 那时候我总是不太记得锁门。

cues.en: And there's a time I was sleeping on kind of a cheap
cues.zh: 有一段时间，我睡在一张挺便宜的

cues.en: mattress that's on one of those cheap bed frames with the
cues.zh: 床垫上，底下是那种带脚轮的

cues.en: casters on it.
cues.zh: 廉价床架。

cues.en: And there was a gap between my bed and the
cues.zh: 我的床和墙之间有一道缝隙，

cues.en: wall that's about this big.
cues.zh: 大概就这么大。

cues.en: I very slowly slid into that gap.
cues.zh: 我非常缓慢地滑进了那道缝里。

cues.en: I pulled the blankets up over my head, and I just held my
cues.zh: 我用毯子蒙住头，屏住

cues.en: breath while Bill walked into my living room, and he
cues.zh: 呼吸，这时 Bill 走进了我的客厅，他

cues.en: his head in my bedroom, and then he walked into the office and then left.
cues.zh: 探头看了看我的卧室，然后走进办公室，接着就离开了。

cues.en: That's what shame feels like. I failed out, I moved back home, went to Indianapolis,
cues.zh: 那就是羞耻的感觉。我被退学了，搬回了家，去了印第安纳波利斯，

cues.en: lived with my parents again, I started doing freelance work, actually signed up
cues.zh: 又和父母住在一起，我开始做自由职业，其实还报名了

cues.en: for classes at a college there. After six months or so it became pretty
cues.zh: 当地一所大学的课程。大约六个月后，情况变得很

cues.en: obvious I just wasn't going to be able to physically or mentally do that, so I
cues.zh: 明显，无论在身体上还是精神上我都撑不下去，于是我

cues.en: lied to my parents, I told them I graduated, and I just came clean on
cues.zh: 对父母撒了谎，说我毕业了，而这件事我大概

cues.en: that one about four years ago or so, and it was so frustrating because even when
cues.zh: 四年前才向他们坦白。这真的让人非常沮丧，因为就算

cues.en: I wanted to, even when I would go to class, I couldn't focus. Even when I
cues.zh: 我想学，就算我去上课了，我也无法集中注意力。就算我

cues.en: wanted to do client work, and unless it was two in the morning the night before
cues.zh: 想做客户的项目，可除非是交工前一天夜里两点，

cues.en: the work was due, I couldn't do it. When I got there, when I got focused on stuff,
cues.zh: 否则我根本动不了笔。当我真正进入状态、全神贯注时，

cues.en: I could produce pretty good work, but I just felt like I had no control. And
cues.zh: 我能做出相当不错的东西，但我就是觉得自己完全失控了。

cues.en: there's this verse in the Bible that says, I do not understand what I do. For
cues.zh: 《圣经》里有这么一节经文说：“我所做的，我自己不明白；因为

cues.en: But what I want to do, I do not do.
cues.zh: 我所愿意的，我并不做。”

cues.en: But instead, that which I hate, I do.
cues.zh: 反而，我厌恶的事，我却去做了。

cues.en: And that's what it felt like.
cues.zh: 当时就是这种感觉。

cues.en: Felt like anything that I tried to do, even the simplest task,
cues.zh: 感觉不管我尝试做什么，哪怕是最简单的事，

cues.en: it felt like I was walking through a swimming pool.
cues.zh: 都像是在游泳池里艰难前行。

cues.en: Like, I just couldn't force myself.
cues.zh: 就像我根本无法强迫自己。

cues.en: I didn't have control.
cues.zh: 我失控了。

cues.en: I was like, why is this?
cues.zh: 我想，怎么会这样？

cues.en: Why can't I control myself?
cues.zh: 我为什么控制不了自己？

cues.en: And so I did what you do, and you have a question
cues.zh: 于是我做了大家有疑问

cues.en: and need an answer to it.
cues.zh: 且急需答案时都会做的事。

cues.en: I Googled it.
cues.zh: 我 Google 了一下。

cues.en: One night, it was like 2 AM, just out of desperation,
cues.zh: 那天晚上，大概凌晨两点，绝望之下，

cues.en: I Googled chronic procrastination.
cues.zh: 我 Google 了“长期拖延症”。

cues.en: And it wasn't long before I was reading about attention deficit disorder.
cues.zh: 没过多久，我就看到了关于注意力缺陷障碍的内容。

cues.en: And I had always kind of joked that I had ADD, but I never meant it.
cues.zh: 我以前总开玩笑说自己有 ADD，但从没当真过。

cues.en: Because ADD is what lazy people use as an excuse because they don't want to work hard
cues.zh: 因为 ADD 是懒人不想努力时用的借口，

cues.en: and that's not me.
cues.zh: 而我根本不是那样的人。

cues.zh: 但我读过一个叫 Tom Hartman 的人写的一本书，叫《爱迪生基因》，他的前提假设

cues.en: was that ADD is genetic and that inventors and creators have it, it's common.
cues.zh: 是注意缺陷障碍（ADD）是遗传的，发明家和创造者往往都有，这很常见。

cues.en: And he said that tens of thousands of years ago,
cues.zh: 他说在几万年前，

cues.en: we had hunters and we had farmers or gatherers.
cues.zh: 我们有人是猎人，有人是农夫或采集者。

cues.zh: 要想成为一名优秀的猎人，

cues.en: you need to go out into new territory every day.
cues.zh: 你每天都得去往新的领地。

cues.en: And you need to be constantly scanning the horizon
cues.zh: 你必须时刻扫视地平线，

cues.en: and able to shift your focus from this thing
cues.zh: 并且能够迅速将注意力从眼前的事物

cues.en: to whatever comes into your peripheral vision
cues.zh: 转移到余光中出现的任何动静上，

cues.en: and rapidly shift.
cues.zh: 进行快速切换。

cues.en: In order to be a farmer,
cues.zh: 而要想成为一名农夫，

cues.en: you just have to be good at doing the same thing
cues.zh: 你只需要擅长重复做同一件事，

cues.en: every single day.
cues.zh: 日复一日。

cues.en: You have to be methodical about it.
cues.zh: 你必须做事有条不紊。

cues.en: And neither skill is better or worse than the other.
cues.zh: 这两种技能并没有孰优孰劣之分。

cues.en: It's just that over time, as civilizations grew, farmers became much more useful than
cues.zh: 只不过随着时间的推移，文明不断发展，农夫变得远比猎人

cues.en: hunters because you can support larger population bases, and when we'd go to war, it'd be the
cues.zh: 更有用，因为你能养活更大规模的人口基数；而一旦发生战争，往往是那些

cues.en: hunters who would go off and get killed, and so their genes would be removed from
cues.zh: 猎人奔赴前线战死，因此他们的基因

cues.en: the pool much more quickly.
cues.zh: 从基因库中被淘汰的速度要快得多。

cues.en: And over time, that portion of the population dropped, and now it's estimated about 10
cues.zh: 随着时间的推移，这一群体的比例有所下降，如今估计约有10%

cues.en: to 20% of the population could probably be diagnosed with ADD.
cues.zh: 到20%的人群可能会被确诊为ADD（注意缺陷障碍）。

cues.en: He talked in that book about how people with ADD are just non-linear thinkers,
cues.zh: 他在书中提到，有ADD的人只是非线性思维者，

cues.en: and people with that don't have ADD are more linear thinkers. And what I found
cues.zh: 而没有ADD的人则更倾向于线性思维。其中让我觉得

cues.en: most encouraging about this is he said that the symptoms that we attribute to
cues.zh: 最受鼓舞的是，他说我们归结于

cues.en: people with ADD, things like lack of focus or procrastination or
cues.zh: ADD患者身上的那些症状，比如注意力不集中、拖延、

cues.en: indecisiveness, those symptoms disappear during periods of high pressure, 2 a.m.
cues.zh: 或优柔寡断，在高压状态下——比如论文截止前的凌晨两点——

cues.en: for the papers do.
cues.zh: 都会烟消云散。

cues.en: Those same symptoms appear in linear thinkers
cues.zh: 而那些同样的症状，反倒会在同样的高压时期

cues.en: during the same periods of high pressure.
cues.zh: 出现在线性思维者身上。

cues.en: So you have to take a linear thinker
cues.zh: 所以只要找一个线性思维的人，

cues.en: and you put them into a high pressure situation,
cues.zh: 把他放进高压环境里，

cues.en: and they will exhibit indecisiveness.
cues.zh: 他就会表现出优柔寡断。

cues.en: They will have a hard time focusing.
cues.zh: 他们很难集中注意力。

cues.en: And I found this really encouraging,
cues.zh: 这让我深受鼓舞，

cues.en: because it wasn't that I was broken.
cues.zh: 因为并不是我这个人坏掉了。

cues.en: It's just that in our society, we've built it.
cues.zh: 只是在如今的社会中，我们把它构建成了这样。

cues.en: So we don't have a lot of high pressure situations.
cues.zh: 所以我们面对的高压情境并不多。

cues.en: If you want to play nice with everyone else these days,
cues.zh: 如今如果你想融入大家，

cues.zh: 就必须得擅长准时上班，

cues.en: every single day at the same time.
cues.zh: 每天都在同一时间打卡。

cues.en: You need to be good at paying your bills
cues.zh: 你得擅长按时付账单，

cues.en: So I kind of accepted this.
cues.zh: 所以我算是接受了这个事实。

cues.en: Because punctuation, the name's for punctuation's long, so we don't say exclamation mark. We
cues.zh: 因为标点符号的名字太长了，所以我们不叫感叹号。我们

cues.en: say? We don't say question mark. It's an underscore, but it's a skid, is what he taught me. And
cues.zh: 叫什么？我们也不叫问号。那是下划线，但他教我叫它滑标（skid）。而且

cues.en: we don't say pound sign. We say octothorpe. I never got that. I never understood it. So
cues.zh: 我们不叫井号。我们叫 octothorpe。我从来没搞懂过。我一直不明白。所以

cues.en: we got two commonly accepted monosyllabic names for that piece of punctuation we call
cues.zh: 对那个标点符号，我们有两个通用的单音节叫法，结果却叫它

cues.en: an octothorpe. It's just a badass name, I guess. A couple weeks after we started working
cues.zh: octothorpe。我觉得这名字听起来挺酷的吧。在我们开始合作

cues.en: and force Caleb started calling in sick.
cues.zh: 几个星期后，Caleb 就开始请病假了。

cues.en: And he started showing up late.
cues.zh: 而且他开始迟到。

cues.en: The excuse was a little different every time,
cues.zh: 每次借口都还不太一样，

cues.en: and it just felt way too familiar to me.
cues.zh: 这让我觉得似曾相识。

cues.en: And I told him my story, and I kind of pulled him aside.
cues.zh: 我就跟他讲了我的经历，并把他拉到一边。

cues.en: And I was just like, you know, what's going on?
cues.zh: 我就问他，你懂的，到底怎么回事？

cues.en: And he said, yeah, you know, I've
cues.zh: 他说，对啊，其实

cues.en: kind of wondered for a while if I have something like that.
cues.zh: 我也怀疑自己是不是也有类似的问题有一阵子了。

cues.en: He's like, well, what am I going to do?
cues.zh: 他又说，那我该怎么办呢？

cues.en: It's not like I'm just going to cold call
cues.zh: 我总不能直接照着黄页

cues.en: psychiatrists from the Yellow Pages.
cues.zh: 给精神科医生挨个打电话吧。

cues.en: So I gave him a couple of names, and he called around.
cues.zh: 于是我给了他几个名字，他就到处去联系了。

cues.en: and it took a little bit of time because it's hard to get availability sometimes.
cues.zh: 这花了一点时间，因为有时候很难约到号。

cues.en: But he got an appointment set up with a psychiatrist for a few weeks out.
cues.zh: 但他还是约到了几周后的精神科门诊。

cues.en: His appointment was set up for a Friday.
cues.zh: 他的预约是在一个周五。

cues.en: The day before that, he sent an email to the team that we were working on,
cues.zh: 就在前一天，他给我们合作的团队发了封邮件，

cues.en: and he said he was sick, he'd seen a doctor tomorrow, he wouldn't be,
cues.zh: 说自己病了，明天要去看医生，来不了，

cues.en: and then he sent me an email.
cues.zh: 接着他又给我发了封邮件。

cues.en: And I just said, hey, I'm having a rough couple of days.
cues.zh: 说，嗨，我这几天状态很糟糕。

cues.en: And he said, right now, I'm just struggling with a lot of things in my head
cues.zh: 他说，我现在脑子里有很多事情在挣扎，

cues.en: and my emotions kept me up the last two nights and that in turn has taken toll on me mentally
cues.zh: 这几晚的情绪让我整整两夜没合眼，反过来也严重消耗了我的精力，

cues.en: and on my mental and physical capacity this morning. I'm scared that if I come into work
cues.zh: 今天早上我的精神和体力都很吃不消。我很害怕如果来上班，

cues.en: I'm going to make a fool of myself with our guests today. I think it would be better if
cues.zh: 会在今天的客人面前出丑。我觉得最好

cues.en: I just focus on making it to my appointment tomorrow.
cues.zh: 还是专心准备明天的看诊。

cues.en: He didn't make it to his appointment.
cues.zh: 他没去赴约。

cues.en: We found out later that he had run out of money.
cues.zh: 后来我们才知道他的钱花光了。

cues.en: And the day after that, he died of an overdose.
cues.zh: 就在那之后第二天，他因药物过量去世了。

cues.en: It was an unintentional overdose.
cues.zh: 那是意外过量。

cues.en: We're quite certain.
cues.zh: 我们非常确定。

cues.en: He called 911 from his phone and he died at the hospital.
cues.zh: 他用手机拨打了 911，然后在医院去世了。

cues.en: And his roommate, who was the first to his apartment after,
cues.zh: 事后第一个赶到他公寓的室友

cues.en: said it was set up just like he was settling in
cues.zh: 说房间里的样子就像他正准备

cues.en: for a Saturday night.
cues.zh: 好好享受一个周六夜晚。

cues.en: He had his video game controller on one side of his couch
cues.zh: 他沙发的一侧放着游戏手柄，

cues.en: and an open pack of Oreos and can of Dr. Pepper on the other.
cues.zh: 另一侧是一包开着的奥利奥和一罐 Dr Pepper。

cues.en: Apparently, he had had a struggle with addiction for quite a while.
cues.zh: 显然，他与成瘾抗争了相当长一段时间。

cues.en: Some of his friends knew about it.
cues.zh: 他的一些朋友是知情的。

cues.en: We didn't.
cues.zh: 我们却不知道。

cues.en: His friend said the problem was Caleb was just so damn smart, he was really good at
cues.zh: 他的朋友说，问题在于 Caleb 实在太聪明了，他特别擅长

cues.en: covering it up and making it seem like it was worse or it wasn't so bad.
cues.zh: 掩饰这一切，让人觉得情况并没那么糟糕。

cues.en: The thing that pisses me off most about this is that Caleb died of an overdose on speed.
cues.zh: 最让我愤怒的是，Caleb 死于安非他命过量。

cues.en: Speed is an amphetamine.
cues.zh: 安非他命是一种苯丙胺。

cues.en: And the meds that are prescribed to me for my ADD are dextro amphetamine.
cues.zh: 而医生给我开的治 ADD 的药，就是右旋苯丙胺。

cues.en: I'm quite certain that Caleb died of self-medicating and untreated mental illness.
cues.zh: 我敢肯定，Caleb 的死是因为自行服药以及未得到治疗的心理疾病。

cues.en: The history of computer science is too littered with tragedies like this.
cues.zh: 计算机科学的历史上充斥着太多这样的悲剧。

cues.en: Alan Turing, the father of computer science, committed suicide after facing intense persecution
cues.zh: 计算机科学之父 Alan Turing，在遭受了残酷的迫害后自杀，

cues.en: from his government.
cues.zh: 迫害他的正是他自己的政府。

cues.en: And earlier this year, we lost Aaron Schwartz to similar circumstances.
cues.zh: 今年早些时候，Aaron Swartz 也因类似的境遇离开了我们。

cues.en: In 2007, Aaron Shorts wrote this.
cues.zh: 2007 年，Aaron Swartz 写下了这样一段话。

cues.en: He said, I have a lot of illnesses.
cues.zh: 他说，我身患多种疾病。

cues.en: I don't talk about it much for a variety of reasons.
cues.zh: 出于种种原因，我很少谈及此事。

cues.en: I feel ashamed to have an illness.
cues.zh: 生病让我感到羞耻。

cues.en: It sounds absurd, but there's still enormous stigma around being sick.
cues.zh: 听起来很荒唐，但生病这件事依然承受着巨大的社会污名。

cues.en: I don't want to use being ill as an excuse,
cues.zh: 我不想拿生病当借口，

cues.en: although sometimes I wonder how much more productive I'd be if I wasn't so sick.
cues.zh: 尽管有时我也会想，如果没病得这么重，我能多出多少成果。

cues.en: Surely there have been times when you have been sad.
cues.zh: 你肯定也曾有过悲伤的时刻。

cues.en: Perhaps a loved one has abandoned you or a plan has gone horribly awry.
cues.zh: 也许是所爱之人离你而去，或是计划彻底泡了汤。

cues.en: Your face falls, perhaps you cry, you feel worthless.
cues.zh: 你耷拉着脸，也许还流了泪，觉得自己一无是处。

cues.en: You wonder whether it's worth going on.
cues.zh: 你甚至怀疑活下去是否还有意义。

cues.en: Everything you think about feels bleak.
cues.zh: 你脑海中的一切都显得灰暗无比。

cues.en: The things you've done, the things you hope to do, the people around you,
cues.zh: 你做过的事、你渴望做的事，还有你身边的人，

cues.en: you lie in bed and want to keep the lights off.
cues.zh: 你躺在床上，只想把灯都关掉。

cues.en: Depressed mood is like that only it doesn't come for any reason
cues.zh: 抑郁的情绪正是如此，只是它来得毫无缘由，

cues.en: and it doesn't go for any either.
cues.zh: 走得也同样莫名其妙。

cues.en: Go outside and get some fresh air, cuddle with a loved one,
cues.zh: 走到室外呼吸新鲜空气，或是与爱人相拥，

cues.en: and you don't feel any better,
cues.zh: 你却丝毫感觉不到好转，

cues.en: only more upset at being unable to feel the joy
cues.zh: 反而因为无法感受到别人似乎都能拥有的快乐，

cues.en: that everyone else seems to feel.
cues.zh: 而感到更加沮丧。

cues.en: Everything gets colored by the sadness.
cues.zh: 一切都被悲伤蒙上了阴影。

cues.en: Depression causes nearly half of all disability.
cues.zh: 抑郁症导致了近一半的残障。

cues.en: It affects one in six
cues.zh: 它影响着六分之一的人，

cues.en: and explains more current unhappiness and poverty.
cues.zh: 也是当下更多不幸与贫困的原因。

cues.en: Sadly, depression, like other mental illnesses,
cues.zh: 令人遗憾的是，抑郁症和其他精神疾病一样，

cues.en: especially addiction, is not seen as real enough
cues.zh: 尤其是成瘾，并没有被认为足够真实，

cues.en: to deserve the investment and awareness
cues.zh: 以至于无法获得像乳腺癌那样

cues.en: of conditions like breast cancer,
cues.zh: 应有的投资与关注度，

cues.en: which affects one in eight,
cues.zh: 尽管乳腺癌影响着八分之一的人，

cues.en: or AIDS, which affects one in 150.
cues.zh: 或是艾滋病，影响着一百五十分之一的人。

cues.en: And there is, of course, the shame.
cues.zh: 当然，还有那种羞耻感。

cues.en: The shame is what's killing us.
cues.zh: 正是这种羞耻感在吞噬我们。

cues.en: And the shame and the stigma around mental illness
cues.zh: 对心理疾病的羞耻感和污名化，

cues.en: is why our coworkers and our friends are suffering from this.
cues.zh: 正是我们的同事和朋友深陷痛苦的原因。

cues.en: If I stood up here and I told you guys that I had cancer,
cues.zh: 如果我站在这里告诉大家我得了癌症，

cues.en: I wouldn't be afraid that anyone would think,
cues.zh: 我绝不会担心有人会觉得，

cues.en: oh, it's just all in his head.
cues.zh: 哦，这全是他自己胡思乱想出来的。

cues.en: If I told you that I took insulin,
cues.zh: 如果我告诉大家我注射胰岛素，

cues.en: no one would say,
cues.zh: 也不会有人对我说：

cues.en: aren't you afraid that you're going to be dependent on that for the rest of your life?
cues.zh: 难道你不担心下半辈子都要依赖它吗？

cues.en: No one would think that I was using it as a crutch.
cues.zh: 没人会觉得我是在找借口逃避。

cues.en: If I broke my leg, no one would say, just try harder.
cues.zh: 如果我摔断了腿，绝不会有人说“你再努力撑撑就行了”。

cues.en: They'd say, go see a doctor.
cues.zh: 他们肯定会说：“快去看医生。”

cues.en: But we have different rules for how we perceive illnesses that affect the brain
cues.zh: 但我们对待大脑疾病的标准，

cues.en: than we do for anything else,
cues.zh: 却和对待其他任何疾病都截然不同，

cues.en: which is ironic because the brain is actually the most complicated organ in the human body.
cues.zh: 这很讽刺，因为大脑其实是人体中最复杂的器官。

cues.en: And yet, so many of us are reluctant to use modern medical advances
cues.zh: 然而，我们当中却有这么多人不愿借助现代医学的发展，

cues.en: to help cure the illnesses that affect it.
cues.zh: 来帮助治愈大脑方面的疾病。

cues.en: I think this is particularly true for developers, because we spent so much of our life being
cues.zh: 我觉得这对开发者来说尤为明显，因为在很大一部分人生中，

cues.en: praised for how well our brain works, that the idea that it could possibly be misfunctioning
cues.zh: 我们都因脑子聪明而备受称赞，所以一旦想到它可能会出故障，

cues.en: threatens our identity and our self-worth.
cues.zh: 就会危及我们的自我认同和个人价值。

cues.en: I can understand why, if you feel like you're struggling with this stuff, you might be reluctant
cues.zh: 我完全理解，如果你觉得自己正受困于这些问题，你可能会有些抗拒，

cues.en: to go see someone or reluctant to take meds.
cues.zh: 不想去看心理医生，也不愿服药。

cues.en: It took me a year from self-diagnosing myself with ADD to seek someone.
cues.zh: 从自我诊断出患有 ADD 到去寻求专业帮助，我花了一年时间。

cues.en: It took me two years after having a medical professional tell me that I had bipolar to go get treatment for it. I get that.
cues.zh: 在医生确诊我患有双相情感障碍后，我花了两年才去接受治疗。我懂那种感受。

cues.en: I was afraid that it would affect the parts of my brain that made me really good at what I do.
cues.zh: 我当时害怕这会影响我大脑中让我擅长自己工作的那部分能力。

cues.en: I was afraid that it would rob me of my creativity. And yes, it's true. My brain works differently now.
cues.zh: 我害怕它会剥夺我的创造力。是的，确实如此，我现在的大脑运转方式变了。

cues.en: I code differently now. I no longer am consumed by thoughts and stay up all night and pull these coding benders and crank stuff out.
cues.zh: 我现在写代码的方式也不同了。我不再被各种思绪吞噬，不再通宵达旦地疯狂写代码来赶工。

cues.en: I'm now much more like the tortoise.
cues.zh: 我现在更像那只乌龟了。

cues.en: I can be measured, I can have an objective view
cues.zh: 我可以更有条理，可以客观地看待

cues.en: of the ideas that they come in
cues.zh: 涌现出来的各种想法，

cues.en: and I have control over them.
cues.zh: 并且能够掌控它们。

cues.en: And most importantly, I am now dependable and reliable,
cues.zh: 最重要的是，我现在变得靠谱、值得信赖了，

cues.en: which is something that I've never been able
cues.zh: 而这是我以前从来无法

cues.en: to tell my friends or to feel like I had before.
cues.zh: 向朋友承诺，或觉得自己具备的特质。

cues.en: going to see a therapist or a psychiatrist has a lot of stigma around it,
cues.zh: 去看心理咨询师或精神科医生总会引来偏见，

cues.en: and I don't get that.
cues.zh: 我实在无法理解。

cues.en: Michael Jordan had a coach.
cues.zh: Michael Jordan 也有教练，

cues.en: Tiger Woods had a coach.
cues.zh: Tiger Woods 也有教练。

cues.en: Why would you not want an objective third party
cues.zh: 为什么你就不想要一个客观的第三方呢？

cues.en: whose job is to shut up and sit there and listen to you,
cues.zh: 对方的职责就是坐在那儿闭嘴倾听，

cues.en: and then occasionally make suggestions?
cues.zh: 然后偶尔提提建议：

cues.en: Maybe you should try doing this just a little bit differently.
cues.zh: “也许你可以试着换个方式来做这件事。”

cues.en: And just as an aside, you have no mental health problems,
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，即便你没有任何心理健康问题，

cues.en: any of you guys are married up there,
cues.zh: 在座各位只要是结了婚的，

cues.en: Go see Get Matter for Counseling.
cues.zh: 都去做做婚姻咨询吧。

cues.en: Rachel and I have been doing this for about a year.
cues.zh: 我和 Rachel 已经做了一年左右。

cues.en: It's like you get a fight with a referee in the room.
cues.zh: 这感觉就像在有裁判在场的情况下吵架。

cues.en: It's amazing.
cues.zh: 太棒了。

cues.en: It's had a huge impact on us.
cues.zh: 这对我们产生了巨大的影响。

cues.en: Even if there's no acute problems, just go see someone.
cues.zh: 即使没有什么严重问题，去找个人聊聊也是好的。

cues.en: It will help.
cues.zh: 真的会有帮助。

cues.en: Finding a therapist is hard.
cues.zh: 找个合适的咨询师确实很难。

cues.en: They tend to be a little bit less tech savvy than we are.
cues.zh: 他们往往不如我们这么懂技术。

cues.en: They tend to operate more by phone than email.
cues.zh: 他们往往更习惯打电话，而不是发邮件。

cues.en: If you go to my blog, boggess.com slash depression,
cues.zh: 如果你去我的博客 boggess.com/depression，

cues.en: There will be some resources on there that you can look up.
cues.zh: 上面会有一些你可以查阅的资源。

cues.en: Unfortunately, I'm not from here, so I can't give any personal recommendations for people
cues.zh: 遗憾的是，我不是本地人，所以没法给这边的朋友

cues.en: in this area, but there are some resources on there that will help you find someone.
cues.zh: 做任何个人推荐，但上面的资源可以帮你找到合适的人。

cues.en: If you're not there yet, just talk to people.
cues.zh: 如果你还没准备好走到那一步，那就先找人聊聊。

cues.en: If you can't find anyone else, talk to me.
cues.zh: 要是找不到其他人，来找我聊。

cues.en: If you feel like you're struggling with this stuff, just let your friends know.
cues.zh: 如果你觉得自己正在受这些困扰，就告诉你的朋友。

cues.en: If you have struggled with this stuff, you can subtly let people know, and you're going
cues.zh: 如果你曾经经历过这些，也可以委婉地告诉大家，

cues.en: to be surprised how many people say, yeah, me too.
cues.zh: 你会惊讶地发现，竟然有那么多人会说：“我也是。”

cues.en: and the things seem so bleak for you right now and you feel like it's not
cues.zh: 如果现在对你来说一切都显得那么灰暗，你觉得情况

cues.en: gonna get better. Just know that 10 years ago I was at college laying in bed
cues.zh: 不会好转了。请记住，十年前我也曾躺在大学宿舍的床上，

cues.en: at night and I was praying that God wouldn't wake me up in the morning. Six
cues.zh: 在深夜里祈祷上帝别再让我于清晨醒来。六年前，

cues.en: years ago I had one dollar in my pocket and no hot water in my apartment and
cues.zh: 我兜里只剩一块钱，公寓里连热水都没有，

cues.en: today I'm standing on stage at Mountain West Ruby, my beautiful wife in the front
cues.zh: 而今天，我站在 Mountain West Ruby 的舞台上，美丽的妻子就坐在第一排。

cues.en: row. Things get better, we just need to start talking about it more. Thank you
cues.zh: 一切都会好起来的，我们只需要开始多谈谈它。谢谢，

cues.en: Thank you very much.
cues.zh: 非常感谢大家。
